o.text: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish آلمان (alman), from French Allemand.

From Proto-Turkic *biĺč- (“to become boiled, to ripe”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (bış-, “to ripen, be cooked”), Turkish pişmek (“to be cooked, baked, roasted”) Bashkir бешеү (bişiw, “to boil, cook”), Chuvash пиҫ (piś, “to boil, stew, cook, ripen”), Kazakh пісу (pisüw, “to mature”), Khakas пызарға (pızarğa, “to ripen, stew, cook, sweat”), Kyrgyz бышуу (bışuu, “to mature, ripen”), Turkmen bişmek (“to be cooked”), Uyghur پىشماق (pishmaq), Yakut бус (bus, “to cook, boil, be ready to eat, ripen”).
almaq (“to buy”) + -ın (“[passive suffix]”). The sense 'to succeed, to work out' is likely a semantic loan from Russian получи́ться (polučítʹsja)/получа́ться (polučátʹsja).
Borrowed from Persian حکایت, from Arabic حِكَايَة (ḥikāya). Doublet of hekayə.
